# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to establish communication first. I can see the bomb but can't hear anything, so I can gesture to Mute (who can see gestures but can't touch the bomb) but I cannot reach the Blind monkey directly with gestures since Blind cannot see. Let me think about the chain: I speak/gesture → Mute receives both. Blind only receives my speech (since Blind cannot see gestures). So I can speak to Blind directly, and gesture+speak to Mute.

Since this is turn 1 and I'm last in speaking order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), I have no prior context yet. Let me report what I see, using speech so Blind can also receive it, since Blind cannot see gestures but can hear speech.

I'll describe the display, light, and wires clearly via speech so both Mute and Blind get the information.

```
speak(text="Deaf report: Display shows number 3. Light is green. Wires are position 1 blue, position 2 yellow, position 3 green.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute sent me a gesture: ✌ (two fingers/peace sign). Since Mute can't speak, and can only communicate to me via gesture (since I can see), this is likely encoding something from the manual - maybe a number, a step, or a reference. I have no other context yet to interpret this.

I should acknowledge receipt and perhaps try to establish a shared understanding. Since I don't know what ✌ means yet, I'll wait for more context or try to prompt clarification. But I can't ask questions via speech to Mute in a way that gets answered quickly since Mute can't speak - Mute can only gesture back, and gestures from Mute would come in future turns.

Let me continue sharing bomb details in case that helps, and acknowledge the gesture so Mute knows I saw it, though acknowledgment doesn't help much. Best to just relay info and wait for pattern to emerge across turns.

```
speak(text="Deaf again: I received a gesture, two fingers, but I do not yet know what it means. Display still 3, light green, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

I used an invalid symbol. I need to pick from the allowed alphabet only. Let me use a simple gesture to signal "unclear/repeat" - I'll just use a distinctive symbol like 🤔... no, not in list. I'll use ✋ (stop/wait) to signal "unclear, please clarify" or pick two different symbols to distinguish from Mute's own signals.

Let me just gesture back something simple to acknowledge, and rely on speech to explain to Mute (since Mute can hear).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf: I see your gestures but do not know their meaning yet. Please try a different way, or I will just describe the bomb and you tell Blind through some other method.")
speak(text="Deaf: display 3, light green, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute is gesturing to me since Mute can't speak and I'm the one who can see gestures. Mute might be trying to signal something using gesture count/patterns - perhaps encoding manual instructions this way, since Mute cannot speak but knows I can relay info to Blind via speech.

The three ☝ (index finger up, pointing up) might mean "wire 3" or "step 3" or "point at position 3". Given the wires are numbered 1,2,3, and wire 3 is green (matching the light color), this might be significant.

Let me think about this differently. Mute reads the manual. Mute cannot speak or touch bomb. Mute's only way to communicate is gesture, and only I (Deaf) can see gestures. So Mute must relay manual info to me via gestures, and then I relay to Blind via speech (since Blind can hear me).

So Mute is trying to build a gesture code with me. Three ☝ symbols in a row - maybe indicating "wire 3" repeated for emphasis, or a step number, or the count of something in the manual.

Given previous turns: ✌ (2 fingers) then 🤟 (love/rock sign - possibly invalid attempt) then ☝☝☝ (three of same symbol). This looks like Mute might be trying to count/number things - possibly identifying which wire to cut, using repetition of a single symbol to indicate a number.

✌ could mean "2" symbolically (peace sign = 2 fingers). Then attempted something else, now ☝☝☝ = three ☝ = number 3?

This suggests Mute is counting using repeated gestures to indicate numbers, trying to tell me something with number 3. Given the wire 3 is green matching light color, and display shows 3 - maybe manual says "cut the wire matching the display number" and display=3, wire 3 = green.

Let me relay this hypothesis to Blind and confirm interpretation to Mute.

```
speak(text="Deaf: I am seeing repeated gestures from Mute, possibly counting to indicate a number, now three of the same symbol - maybe indicating wire 3 or step 3. Display shows 3, and wire 3 is green, matching the light which is also green. Blind, do not act yet, we are still decoding Mute's signals.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","☝","☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured 👍 (thumbs up) after I echoed back ☝☝☝ (three fingers, indicating wire 3 / number 3). This looks like confirmation - Mute is agreeing with my interpretation that "3" is the correct number/wire.

This makes sense: my hypothesis was that the manual instructs to act on wire matching the display number (3), and wire 3 is green matching the light. Mute's thumbs up confirms this interpretation is correct.

Now I should relay this confirmed instruction to Blind clearly, since Blind is the one who needs to act on the bomb.

```
speak(text="Deaf: Mute confirmed with thumbs up that the number is 3. This matches display 3 and wire 3 which is green, same as the light. Blind, the instruction is likely to cut or act on wire 3, the green wire. Mute, if this is wrong, gesture thumbs down, otherwise thumbs up again to reconfirm.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","☝","☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed again with 👍 (thumbs up). This strongly supports that wire 3 (green) is the correct wire to act on. Time to give Blind a clear final instruction to act, since we have double confirmation from Mute.

```
speak(text="Deaf: Confirmed twice by Mute with thumbs up. Blind, please cut or act on wire 3, the green wire, the one matching the light color and the display number.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```
